newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle crew activates space lab.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle crew activates space lab.

text.p: The crew of the U.S. space shuttle Columbia completed activation of their $86 million space laboratory on Thursday, NASA officials said.
"Things are progressing well and the team is looking forward to another two weeks of science," mission operations director Jeff Bantle told a news conference.
Columbia's seven astronauts, working in a bus-sized laboratory, started up the last of their 33 major scientific experiments overnight.
The shuttle's 16-day mission will investigate fire in space, the manufacture of new alloys and the growth of protein crystals to aid medical research.
Scientists hope the shuttle's combustion experiments will lead to more efficient and cleaner ways of burning fuel.
The reusable solid rocket boosters that helped Columbia soar into space were returned to Cape Canaveral on Wednesday. Initial inspections revealed no unusual damage, NASA spokesman Joel Wells said.
Columbia and its seven astronauts are due back to Earth on July 17.
